title: Dynamic pressure scaler and GPU slot reclamation for sustained high-QPS
creator: Claire Zhang
description: Reduce P95 latency regressions and out-of-memory incidents during sustained high QPS by introducing a Dynamic Pressure Scaler (DPS) and a GPU slot reclamation mechanism. This ticket designs and implements admission controls, probabilistic micro-batch shedding, NVMe spill for cold KV pages, and safe GPU slab compaction to keep latency SLOs while maximizing throughput and utilization.
background: We've observed recurring P95 spikes and occasional OOMs when sustained QPS exceeds the inferred capacity for certain model-VM combinations. Existing micro-batch admission is static and reacts too late; KV cache eviction is LRU-only and moves cold data straight to host memory causing sudden GPU page faults; slab allocator can't compact safely during steady-state. This work is intended to act before tail-latency worsens and avoid hard capacity failures.
goals: Maintain p95 latency <= 350ms at target sustained QPS (per model profile)
Avoid GPU OOMs during 30-minute sustained load tests at 1.5x expected bursting traffic
Keep throughput reduction below 7% compared to baseline under normal load
Provide observable metrics and knobs to tune DPS for customer-specific SLAs
acceptance_criteria: DPS runs in runtime with config flags and exposes headroom and admission rates
Evidence from perfbench: p95 <= 350ms and no OOMs for 30-minute 1.5x sustained QPS test
KV cold pages spill to NVMe with bounded spill latency; end-to-end token latency impact < 10% for affected requests
Canary rollout plan documented and automated via console rollout config
Unit + integration tests and chaos test scenarios added to CI
decisions: Use a hybrid headroom estimator: EWMA of free_gpu_memory_fraction + weighted p95 latency margin to compute available microbatch slots
Admission controller will use probabilistic shedding (token-aware random drop) rather than pure max-queue-length to avoid bias against long requests
KV cache eviction will tier: GPU -> host hot-cache -> NVMe spill. NVMe page metadata kept lightweight to avoid controller lock contention.
GPU slab compaction will be asynchronous and scheduled during detected low-utilization windows; a pre-compaction guard prevents compaction if active_headroom < 1.2x target
tradeoffs: Probabilistic shedding may increase variance for a small fraction of requests but reduces global tail risk compared to heavy-handed queue trimming
NVMe spill adds read latency for cold requests; we accept a small hit for cold paths to preserve hot-path latency and avoid OOMs
Async slab compaction complicates memory accounting and requires conservative thresholds to avoid interfering with hot path. This increases implementation complexity but reduces forced evictions.
progress_updates: 2026-03-01: Ticket created after postmortem for incident #INC-2026-02-17. Assigned to Owen.
2026-03-03: Prototype DPS estimator implemented in a feature branch; initial headroom signal derived from 10s EWMA of free_memory_fraction.
2026-03-05: Integration test added for probabilistic admission with synthetic token-length distribution; observed 4% throughput drop with 60% reduction in long-tail latency.
2026-03-07: NVMe spill shim merged behind feature flag; measured 18ms median spill read plus 80ms tail on cold reads — acceptable for cold paths with cache warming strategy.

2026-03-09: First canary harness (5% traffic) run; no OOMs observed, p95 improved from 520ms -> 320ms for the targeted model at peak load. Some flaky failures around compaction task scheduling remain.
test_plan: Unit tests for headroom estimator edge cases (division by zero, rapid free_memory changes)
Simulated workload: mixed short(<=8 tokens) / long(>256 tokens) requests with realistic inter-arrival times; run 30m at 1.5x expected QPS
Chaos test: kill one GPU worker node while canary is active to validate fallback and KV spill recovery
A/B perfbench against baseline with metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, OOM count, GPU memory fragmentation
Regression test in CI that runs lightweight DPS smoke scenario on PRs
rollout_plan: Feature behind runtime flag and console toggle
Canary 1: 2% traffic for 24h with enhanced logging
Canary 2: 10% traffic for 48h if no regressions
Canary 3: 50% for 72h, monitor p95, OOMs, KV spill rates
Full ramp to 100% after two green canaries and post-rollout review
notes: Follow-up ticket will explore dynamic quantization triggers paired with DPS to reclaim memory during extreme load
Coordinate with Dedicated infra for autoscaler interplay; autoscaler may report capacity that conflicts with DPS heuristics — add a sync hook in a follow-up
Design doc contains an appendix with command-line debugging utilities to inspect headroom signals in production
